elements.evidence: "indemnify Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, losses, costs and expenses"

elements.evidence: "(a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right"

elements.evidence: "(c) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor"

elements.evidence: "content or materials provided by Customer for use in the Services"

elements.element: Customer indemnity limited to Customer's breach of law
elements.evidence: "or Customer's breach of Applicable Law" (no other Customer indemnity triggers)

elements.element: Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications)
elements.evidence: Inserted text contains no exclusions; only "to the extent arising out of" qualifiers
No remedy language; Section 9.3 still refers to "the remedies required by Section 20.5"

elements.element: Vendor indemnity subject to super-cap of 3× annual fees
elements.evidence: No cap language inserted; 21.3 lists "its indemnification obligations" as Excluded Claims without a super-cap

reasons: All atomic elements of the preferred position are present in one concise inserted paragraph: Vendor defence and indemnity of Customer and Affiliates, the four coverage triggers (IP infringement of Services/Deliverables, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct), notice/control/cooperation procedure, and a Customer indemnity narrowed to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of Applicable Law.

Minimality is satisfied: the Agreement had no indemnification article, and the insertion adds no fallback-only material (no procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, no super-cap), no extra indemnitees, no hold-harmless or settlement-consent mechanics.
Fallback is separately incomplete (no usual exclusions, no infringement remedies, no 3× annual fees super-cap), which is acceptable because the locked target is preferred.

Non-blocking note: Sections 9.3 and 30.5 cross-reference "Section 20.5" while the inserted Section 20 is a single unnumbered paragraph; this dangling reference pre-existed the redline, but adding sub-numbering (e.g., 20.5 for infringement remedies) would tidy it.
